target.title: fix(ci): isolate OpenWebUI release smoke
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Full release validation could exhaust the GitHub-hosted runner disk before the Open WebUI image finished pulling. In run https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29036410675 (job `86187259468`), the shared Docker release job had only 49 MB free and failed with `no space left on device`, even though the preceding release lanes had passed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Run Open WebUI as its own stable/full release chunk on the existing `blacksmith-32vcpu-ubuntu-2404` large-disk runner. Keep it out of `plugins-runtime-services`, retain legacy aggregate aliases for manual reruns, and make the dedicated job lean by installing Node/pnpm without Bun, repository dependencies, or a pnpm cache.

The job now propagates the selected release profile and is gated to stable/full profiles, so full artifacts remain labeled `full` and beta coverage does not accidentally acquire a stable-only lane. The reusable runner input documents Open WebUI as an intentional large-disk exception.

## User Impact

Release validation keeps the same Open WebUI compatibility coverage, but the external image no longer competes for disk with package, plugin, and shared Docker images. Targeted Open WebUI reruns and legacy aggregate aliases remain available.

## Evidence

- Testbox-through-Crabbox `tbx_01kx47a9a5bdnr0w44wjqsbzh7`: `pnpm test test/scripts/package-acceptance-workflow.test.ts test/scripts/docker-e2e-plan.test.ts test/scripts/release-workflow-matrix-plan.test.ts test/scripts/test-install-sh-docker.test.ts test/scripts/ci-workflow-guards.test.ts` — 182/182 passed.
- Same Testbox: `pnpm check:workflows` — passed.
- Same Testbox: `pnpm check:changed` — passed.
- Local lightweight checks: actionlint, `git diff --check`, and skill frontmatter YAML parsing — passed.
- Fresh Codex autoreview after the profile-gating fixes: no accepted or actionable findings.
- Tests assert one Open WebUI lane in the full aggregate plan, zero in beta, zero in `plugins-runtime-services`, one in the standalone chunk, one/zero across every legacy plugin aggregate with the option enabled/disabled, the dedicated large-disk runner, lean setup, and exact profile propagation.

The authoritative live Docker proof will run from this exact PR head and again in the final full-release matrix after landing.
